clue.text: One has repulsed British man in authority

indicators.note: repulsed means driven back, so the words before it are read backwards

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone has fought off a British official who wields power over them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'repulsed' turns I HAS round to give SAHI, before B.
explanation.definitionFit: Sahib was the title used in colonial India for a European master or official, a man holding authority.

clue.text: More awkward, erecting harbour's jetty

indicators.note: erecting means setting upright, and in a down clue that reads the word upwards, backwards

parts.note: harbour's, as harbour is, gives PORT'S, read as PORTS
a jetty is a landing pier

explanation.surface: Building a jetty for the harbour is proving ever more troublesome.
explanation.walkthrough: 'erecting' reads the harbour word upwards, as fits a down light; 'harbour's' supplies the plural-looking S.
explanation.definitionFit: Stroppy is British slang for bad-tempered and difficult, so the comparative means more awkward.

clue.text: First sign of hay fever for former Tory leader

indicators.note: the first sign of a word is its opening letter

parts.note: ague is an old word for a malarial fever

explanation.surface: Sneezing is the earliest symptom of hay fever.
explanation.walkthrough: William Hague led the UK Conservative (Tory) party from 1997 to 2001.
explanation.definitionFit: William Hague is a politician who once headed Britain's Conservative party.

clue.text: College dance: I love to meet lecturer

parts.note: a ball is a formal dance
love is nil in tennis scoring, the letter O

explanation.surface: A student invites a lecturer to the college dance.
explanation.definitionFit: Balliol is one of the colleges of Oxford University.

clue.text: Drink milk one restaurant employee put out

parts.note: to milk a source is to tap it

indicators.note: put out means removed, so the numeral is taken from the employee

parts.note: a waiter serves in a restaurant
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: A milky drink annoyed one of the waiting staff.
explanation.walkthrough: 'milk' looks like the drink but is the verb meaning draw off; 'put out' looks like annoyed but means removed.
explanation.definitionFit: Water from the tap is something people drink, as opposed to bottled water.

clue.text: Lionel Richie song: it led Theresa May astray

indicators.note: astray means gone off course, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A pop ballad supposedly led the Prime Minister Theresa May off track.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the title of a 1978 hit ballad by the Commodores, written and sung by Lionel Richie.

clue.text: Brief reference in page one, first bit of book

indicators.note: in places the shortened reference inside the other pieces

parts.note: an ace is the one in a suit of cards
ref is a short form of reference

explanation.surface: A short citation on the first page at the beginning of a book.
explanation.definitionFit: A preface is the introductory section at the opening of a book.

clue.text: Nourishing meat in all stews

indicators.note: stews means cooks into a mixture, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Every stew contains meat, which is good nourishment.
explanation.definitionFit: Alimental means providing food or sustenance, from the same root as alimentary.

clue.text: Acclaim former tax cut

parts.note: ex means former, as in ex-wife

indicators.note: cut means trimmed, so the last letter of the tax is lopped off

parts.note: a toll is a charge or levy

explanation.surface: People cheer the scrapping of an old tax.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut' docks the final L of TOLL to leave TOL.
explanation.definitionFit: To extol is to praise highly, a synonym of acclaim as a verb.

clue.text: It may be on TV for good

parts.note: pro means for, in favour of

explanation.surface: Something shown on television might be a good thing.
explanation.definitionFit: Prog is a short informal form of programme, a show broadcast on television.

clue.text: Thieves worried as clients reserve rights, principally

indicators.note: to reserve is to keep or hold, so the jumble holds the letter inside it
worried means agitated, so these letters are stirred up
principally means first of all, taking the opening letter

explanation.surface: Anxious customers hold back their legal entitlements.
explanation.walkthrough: 'worried' jumbles AS CLIENTS into LACENISTS; 'reserve' has it hold R, the first letter of 'rights'.
explanation.definitionFit: Larceny is theft, so larcenists are people who steal.

clue.text: Primate eats little from abroad … lacking this?

definitions.text: Primate eats little from abroad … lacking this?

indicators.note: eats means takes in, so the French word goes inside the primate

parts.note: an ape is a primate
petit is French for little

explanation.surface: An ape that eats only a tiny amount must be short of hunger.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition: an ape eating little lacks a desire for food.
explanation.definitionFit: Hunger or desire for food is what a creature that eats very little is missing.

clue.text: Antique article, Eastern, coated in precious metal

parts.note: a is the indefinite article

indicators.note: coated in means covered by, so the letter goes inside the metal

parts.note: gold is a precious metal

explanation.surface: An old Oriental object is gilded.
explanation.definitionFit: Something very ancient, centuries old, is antique.

clue.text: Popular fellows on TV broadcast, the reverse of top brain boxes

indicators.note: on means placed after, so the fellows come second, following the television word

parts.note: in means fashionable, popular

indicators.note: broadcast means spoken on air, so the word sounds the same but is written differently

parts.note: telly is British slang for television
gents are men, fellows

indicators.note: the reverse of means read backwards

parts.note: A1 means top-class, written AI in crosswords

explanation.surface: Celebrities on a television show are the opposite of the clever set.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broadcast' gives TELLI, sounding like TELLY; 'the reverse of' turns AI (A1) into IA.
explanation.definitionFit: Brain boxes is a British idiom for clever people; the intelligentsia are a society's intellectual class.

clue.text: Work out two notes will suffice for cost of ticket

parts.note: to work out at the gym is to train
fa and re are two notes of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: Practising two pieces of music will cover the ticket.
explanation.definitionFit: A train fare is the price paid for a rail ticket.

clue.text: Rising of Middle Eastern soldiers leading to end of conflict soon

indicators.note: in a down clue rising means read upwards, backwards

parts.note: Omani means from Oman in the Middle East
men are soldiers

indicators.note: end of means the last letter

explanation.surface: An uprising of Arab troops brings a war to a close.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rising of' sends OMANI upwards in the down light as INAMO.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means very shortly, before long, which is soon.

clue.text: Terrorist shot Bulgarian ruler

indicators.note: shot means broken or ruined, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A gunman assassinated the leader of Bulgaria.
explanation.definitionFit: An urban guerrilla is an insurgent who carries out violent attacks in cities.

clue.text: Man stashes weapon inside item of clothing

indicators.note: stashes means hides away, so the man holds the weapon within

parts.note: a gent is a man
an arm is a weapon

explanation.surface: A man hides a gun in his clothes.
explanation.definitionFit: A garment is any article of dress.

clue.text: Mock feeble-sounding event at uni

parts.note: to rag is to tease or mock

indicators.note: sounding says the word for feeble is heard, not spelt

parts.note: weak means feeble

explanation.surface: Students jeer at a lame-sounding campus occasion.
explanation.walkthrough: RAG WEEK is a British student charity fundraising week of stunts and parades.
explanation.definitionFit: Rag week is a regular charity-fundraising festival held by British university students.

clue.text: Key work by Descartes perhaps rejected

parts.note: op is short for opus, a work

indicators.note: rejected means thrown back, so the name is reversed

parts.note: René Descartes is an example of a Rene

explanation.surface: An important work by the French philosopher is turned down.
explanation.definitionFit: A key is a device for unlocking, something that opens a lock.

clue.text: Public relations hoo-ha in Madrid museum

parts.note: ado means fuss, a hoo-ha

explanation.surface: A publicity fuss breaks out at a Spanish gallery.
explanation.definitionFit: The Prado is Spain's national art gallery in Madrid.

clue.text: No lager drunk by northern chap

indicators.note: drunk means intoxicated, so these letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: A man from the north refuses beer.
explanation.definitionFit: Algernon is a man's first name, so it can stand for a chap.

clue.text: Sussex town reportedly has no money

indicators.note: reportedly means as said aloud, so the town is heard rather than spelt

parts.note: Rye is a small town in East Sussex

explanation.surface: A seaside town in southern England is broke.
explanation.walkthrough: Rye is a historic town in East Sussex, a county on England's south coast.
explanation.definitionFit: Rhino is old British slang for cash.

clue.text: Agrees gala could turn out to be money-raising event

indicators.note: could turn out means might end up arranged differently, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A committee agrees a fete might become a fundraiser.
explanation.definitionFit: A householder sells unwanted goods from their premises to raise cash at such a sale.

clue.text: Composer introduced by these violinists doing a turn

indicators.note: doing a turn says the hidden letters are read backwards
introduced by means held within, so the name sits inside these words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A composer is presented by violinists who perform a routine.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft took 'Composer introduced' as the definition, but 'introduced by' signals the concealed letters; the definition is 'Composer' alone.
explanation.definitionFit: Charles Ives was an American modernist composer.

clue.text: Go after group of hags in Midlands city

indicators.note: after places the attempt behind the witches

parts.note: a coven is a gathering of witches
a go is a try, an attempt

explanation.surface: Chase after a band of witches in an English city.
explanation.definitionFit: Coventry is a city in the West Midlands of England.

clue.text: Form of punishment, nothing a Northerner would mention

indicators.note: a Northerner would mention means as spoken in a northern voice, so the word is heard

parts.note: nowt is northern English dialect for nothing

explanation.surface: A northern person says there is no penalty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nowt' is northern English for nothing; with its silent K the answer is said the same way.
explanation.definitionFit: A knout was a whip used for flogging in imperial Russia.
